text:
support-ops: FYI incoming customer escalation — Acme reported intermittent 5xx and a bunch of client timeouts hitting hosted API since ~08:00 UTC. They see a flurry of 504s and long p95s.

cleo-cs: Customer says their batch job suddenly spiked and now ~10% of calls are 504/timeout. Provided example request_id=rid_20240308_abc123 and a couple of screenshots.

support-ops: Logged original support ticket 12345, attaching link to request traces. @nina.sre can you triage whether this is our gateway or downstream batcher backlog?

nina.sre: looking. Initial signal: request_queue_depth for tenant acme-prod jumped from 40 -> 180 in ~30s. Continuous-batcher backlog metric continuous_batch_pending jumped and didn't drain. Gateway returned 504 with message "dequeue timeout".

sre-bot: Alert fired: hosted.gateway.request_queue_depth > 150 (5m avg) for tenant=acme-prod.

mike-plat: That smells like queue saturation + longseq tasks preventing batch dequeue. Any long-sequence requests in traces?

nina.sre: Yes — traces show a cluster of requests with seq_len ~4096 that stay in batch for >6s. Worker_kv_cache misses increased, and batch formation times jumped.

jamie-devex: Customer note: their SDK retries on 5xx aggressive defaults. They did a 10x retry loop which could amplify the backlog.

cleo-cs: They say they only upgraded to a new model variant ~07:50 UTC; might be a heavier model with slower per-token.

nina.sre: Repro steps I'm running locally (quick script) — concurrent 250 POSTs with long sequences + SDK retry = reproduces queue pileup and 504 wave. Example curl (sanitized):

```
# simple repro (do not run on prod)
for i in {1..250}; do 
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.internal/v1/generate \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
    -d '{"model":"acme-heavy","input":"'$(printf 'x%.0s' {1..4000})'"}' &
done; wait
```

mike-plat: Good repro. What metrics to watch while we mitigate? I suggest request_queue_depth, continuous_batch_pending, batch_formation_time_ms, kv_cache_miss_rate, and gateway_dequeue_timeouts.

nina.sre: Immediate mitigations proposed: 1) throttle tenant via rate-limit to reduce enqueue pressure, 2) switch tenant to smaller model variant (acme-medium) temporarily, 3) increase dequeue workers on the affected pool, 4) bump queue depth soft limit to allow graceful draining — but that has risk of longer overall latency.

support-ops: Which is fastest to apply?

mike-plat: Throttle is fastest — apply a tenant-level rate cap at the ingress proxy for acme-prod to match baseline TPS. I can roll a short-lived rule. Also can enable automatic fallback to acme-medium (if model routing policy exists).

nina.sre: I'll also scale up batcher workers for that pool by +50% (kubectl scale deployment batcher-acme --replicas=N). It should help as long as GPU slots are free.

cleo-cs: Customer asked for ETA. Can we confirm a temporary fix timeline?

mike-plat: Throttle roll takes ~5m to push. Scale batchers ~10-15m to observe drain. I'll coordinate with infra to ensure capacity.

jamie-devex: Also advise customer to reduce SDK retries and set exponential backoff. Provide recommended client config.

nina.sre: Root cause hypothesis: new heavier model variant increased per-request token time and blocked continuous-batcher drains. Combined with aggressive client retries -> enqueue storm -> queue depth hit -> gateway dequeue timeouts -> 504s. Secondary contributor: kv cache miss spike slowed token generation.

sre-bot: Action created: INCIDENT-2026-311 - Runbook started.

mike-plat: Mitigation steps executed: applied tenant throttle at ingress (limit=80 rps), routed new traffic to acme-medium, scaled batcher-acme replicas +2. Observed continuous_batch_pending falling from 170 -> 30 over 12 minutes.

cleo-cs: Customer confirmed fewer 5xx after your changes. They still want postmortem and options to avoid recurrence.

nina.sre: Follow-ups: - collect full traces for the window 07:45-08:15 UTC, - record exact model commit that was rolled, - run offline load test to measure per-token latency for model variants, - propose a routing policy: heavy models + longseq should go dedicated capacity or limited concurrency.

jamie-devex: I'll draft suggested client SDK defaults (retry backoff, max_concurrency_per_client) and a public KB entry: "Avoiding enqueue storms for long-sequence workloads".

mike-plat: Ops note: consider adding an automatic detection: if continuous_batch_pending grows > threshold and kv_cache_miss_rate high -> trigger temporary circuit-breaker that prevents additional longseq requests from entering the shared pool.

cleo-cs: CS would like a short summary to send to customer: what we did, why it happened, next steps. I'll draft and circulate.

nina.sre: Leaving ownership of postmortem to SRE. I'll include timeline, metric charts, and exact CLI commands we ran. Quick log snippets from gateway at peak: 

```
[2026-03-08T08:02:13Z] WARN tenant=acme-prod dequeue_time_ms=3000 reason=dequeue_timeout queue_len=172
[2026-03-08T08:02:14Z] ERROR tenant=acme-prod gateway_resp=504 request_id=rid_20240308_abc123
```

jamie-devex: Ping me when postmortem drafts exist — I'll convert part to KB.

cleo-cs: Closing customer loop: they requested dedicated capacity options and a checklist for model rollout. We'll propose Dedicated capacity or staged rollout with load tests.

support-ops: Thanks team. Action items summarized: [nina.sre] postmortem + timeline, [mike-plat] propose automated circuit-breaker and draft ingress throttle playbook, [jamie-devex] SDK KB + model rollout checklist, [cleo-cs] customer comms. Marking incident resolved once postmortem is filed. :white_check_mark:
